My favorite Mac transcription tool, MacWhisper, has rolled out another major update today, adding real-time meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker recognition accuracy, and deeper Apple Intelligence integration, along with an all-new transcription model. Here are the highlights of this update.

Deep integration of MacWhisper with Apple Intelligence

I've written many articles about my reliance on MacWhisper, especially in my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the earliest AI transcription tools developed for the Mac platform. Since its launch in 2023 by independent developer Jordi Bruin, it has been continuously improved, with expanding support for new models, services, and workflows.

These improvements include automatic meeting recording, speaker recognition, folder watching, system-wide dictation, local and cloud-based AI models, as well as integration with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper is upgraded to version 15.2, introducing improved speaker recognition powered by NVIDIA's newly released Nemotron 3 speaker diarization model.

This change also brings another major feature in this update: real-time meeting transcription.

This feature has been on MacWhisper's public roadmap for some time and has finally been realized, allowing users to view real-time transcripts, rewind, copy, or send live transcripts during meetings.

As for transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, supporting 22 languages, with deep integration into macOS 27's Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts features.

Now Mac users (including those in the EU) can search transcripts system-wide, open transcripts with Siri, send text to Shortcuts, and reference on-screen transcripts when querying Siri or Apple Intelligence.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folder and subfolder features for organizing transcripts and meeting notes, and supports dragging existing transcript files into folders from the sidebar.
